title: Module 10 Misconception Sort
intro: Decide whether each statement is true, false, or depends. These are the misconceptions that cost students points on exams.

items.s: A significant F means every group differs from every other group.
items.why: It indicates at least one difference. Post hoc tests identify which.
F is a ratio of two variances, which are never negative.

items.s: ANOVA with two groups gives the same conclusion as an independent t test.
items.why: In that case F equals t squared and the p values match.

items.s: A bigger F always means a bigger effect.
items.why: F depends on sample size as well as effect. Use eta squared for the size of the effect.

items.s: When groups differ a lot, MS within gets larger.
items.why: MS within reflects variability among people in the same condition. Group differences raise MS between.

items.s: The total SS equals SS between plus SS within.
items.why: ANOVA partitions the total variability into these two parts.

items.s: You should run Tukey tests regardless of whether F is significant.
items.why: Post hoc tests follow a significant omnibus F.

items.s: ANOVA assumes the populations have equal variances.
items.why: Homogeneity of variance is one of the assumptions, along with independence and approximate normality.
